nodes.description: Because melanosomes do not reach the dendritic tips, transfer of pigment from melanocytes into neighbouring epidermal keratinocytes and into the growing hair shaft is reduced and uneven. Pigment synthesis itself is normal; the defect is in delivery, which is why hair contains a few large irregular melanin clumps rather than evenly dispersed granules and why the skin is lighter than the family background.
nodes.id: Defective Melanosome Transfer to Keratinocytes and Hair

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in Mlph, encoding a member of the Rab effector family, cause the melanosome transport defects observed in leaden mice.
evidence.snippet: All three mutant loci encode genes that are required for the polarized transport of melanosomes, the specialized, pigment-containing organelles of melanocytes, to the neighboring keratinocytes and eventually into coat hairs.

nodes.description: Melanophilin binds GTP-RAB27A on the melanosome through its N-terminal Slp homology domain and the globular tail of myosin Va through its C-terminal half, and also binds actin. It is required for myosin Va to associate with melanosomes. When melanophilin is lost, RAB27A still reaches the melanosome but myosin Va is not recruited, so the organelle is not captured by the peripheral actin network.
nodes.id: Failure of the RAB27A-Melanophilin-Myosin Va Tripartite Complex

animal_models.description: In leaden primary melanocytes myosin Va does not associate with melanosomes although RAB27A does.

evidence.reference_title: Slac2-a/melanophilin, the missing link between Rab27 and myosin Va: implications of a tripartite protein complex for melanosome transport.
evidence.snippet: Deletion analysis and site-directed mutagenesis showed that the N-terminal Slp (synaptotagmin-like protein) homology domain of Slac2-a specifically binds Rab27A/B isoforms and that the C-terminal half directly binds the globular tail of myosin Va.

evidence.reference_title: Melanophilin, the product of the leaden locus, is required for targeting of myosin-Va to melanosomes.
evidence.snippet: The localization of rab27a to melanosomes did not require the function of either myosin-Va or melanophilin, but leaden function was required for the association of myosin-Va with melanosomes.

nodes.description: Diffuse hypopigmentation of the skin relative to unaffected relatives, which can be subtle in lightly pigmented families.

nodes.description: The classical recessive leaden coat-color mutant, caused by Mlph mutations. Leaden mice have a diluted coat with normal melanin synthesis and perinuclear clumping of melanosomes in melanocytes, the same cellular defect as human GS3. Leaden melanocytes were also used to show that melanophilin is required to recruit myosin Va to the melanosome.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in Mlph, encoding a member of the Rab effector family, cause the melanosome transport defects observed in leaden mice.
evidence.snippet: Collectively, our data show that Mlph is a critical component of the melanosome transport machinery and suggest that Mlph might function as part of a transport complex with Rab27a and MyoVa.

evidence.reference_title: Griscelli syndrome restricted to hypopigmentation results from a melanophilin defect (GS3) or a MYO5A F-exon deletion (GS1).
evidence.snippet: We herein present genetic and functional evidence that a third form of GS (GS3), whose expression is restricted to the characteristic hypopigmentation of GS, results from mutation in the gene that encodes melanophilin (Mlph), the ortholog of the gene mutated in leaden mice.

evidence.reference_title: [Griscelli syndrome type 3: A new case].
evidence.snippet: R35W mutation was described in 9 cases and E98X and R35Q mutations were each found in one case.

nodes.description: Biallelic germline MLPH variants remove functional melanophilin. The recurrent p.R35W and the p.D25H missense variants sit in the N-terminal Slp homology (RAB27-binding) domain; p.E98X truncates the protein. In patient melanocytes homozygous for p.R35W, melanophilin protein is almost undetectable, whereas p.D25H leaves protein abundance unchanged and acts through loss of binding instead - two routes to the same functional loss.

evidence.snippet: We herein present genetic and functional evidence that a third form of GS (GS3), whose expression is restricted to the characteristic hypopigmentation of GS, results from mutation in the gene that encodes melanophilin (Mlph), the ortholog of the gene mutated in leaden mice.

evidence.snippet: MLPH protein expression is nearly absent in both GSIII melanocytes lysates (0.65% for DB200 and 3.61% for DB212) compared to control (100%) (Figure 4B).

nodes.description: Homozygous missense (c.73G>C) in the Slp homology domain, reported in a Chinese Han patient from a non-consanguineous family. It reduces RAB27A binding without lowering protein level.

nodes.description: Homozygous missense in the Slp homology domain (c.103C>T, reported as c.102C>T in older nomenclature). Recurrent in Arab and Turkish families; abolishes the RAB27A interaction and leaves almost no melanophilin protein in patient melanocytes.

evidence.reference_title: Cellular and clinical report of new Griscelli syndrome type III cases.

nodes.description: Mature, pigmented melanosomes aggregate around the nucleus of the melanocyte and dendrites and dendritic tips are left depleted of them. This is the cellular hallmark shared by all three Griscelli forms. In GS3 patient melanocytes it is reversed by expressing wild-type melanophilin but not the p.R35W variant.
